experiment_note: Run of codex_think_ec_tools2 (label codex_think_ec_tools2): same model deployment, reasoning_effort and streaming route as codex_think_ec_tools_r2 (the baseline for this comparison, label codex_think_ec_tools_r2, 10 passed / 15 benchmark_failed of 25). Differences, each proven live before this launch: (1) a single string shell(command, workdir?, timeout_ms?) + write_file(path, content) tool contract, no array-form fallback, no silent repair of invalid arguments -- the old fallback accounted for about 6% of all tool calls in r2 and up to 48% of a single trajectory's steps; (2) the submission client has a per-agent front gate (at most 3 concurrent submit clients per container, refused at once, nothing sent, if more are attempted) -- r2 had agents that were rate-limited hundreds of times and one agent OOM-killed by a 500-way submission fan-out; (3) the context-fit (compaction) guarantee now reads the model's real reported token count (the old code silently estimated from characters because the usage-only stream chunk was dropped, and never fired once across r2 despite 7 agents dying on a Bedrock context-length 400), and the compaction summary is now grounded in the task text with a mechanical ledger of commands already run, fixing a measured case of the agent repeating completed work after a compaction. Grading is unchanged in this run (the stricter grading patch is staged, not deployed, pending a separate decision). DSML recovery is removed (the new string contract has no array-vs-string ambiguity for the model to leak).
